name: Tropic Seamount
note: Cobalt-rich crusts and ferromanganese deposits; cold-water coral gardens; bottom-trawling and mining concession overlap.

name: Vema Seamount
note: Endemic Tristan rock lobster fished to commercial extinction in the 1960s–70s; reopened fishing has yet to recover the stock.

name: Ampère Seamount
note: Sub-Mediterranean alboran fauna; Spanish/Portuguese longline and bottom-trawl fleets target alfonsino and orange roughy spawning aggregations.

name: Atlantis Seamount
note: Hydrothermal-influenced seamount with Lophelia pertusa thickets — slow-growing reefs sliced by trawl scars.

name: Walters Shoal
region: SW Indian Ocean, south of Madagascar
note: Isolated shallow peak rising 5 km from abyssal plain; SIODFA voluntary closure ignored by some IUU fleets — endemic species risk extinction.

name: Saya de Malha Bank
note: World's largest seagrass meadow + ancient seamount complex; Sri Lankan and Thai bottom-trawl fleets operate beyond national jurisdiction.

name: Cobb Seamount
note: Pacific rockfish and sablefish hotspot; trawl-closure zone partially enforced — coral gardens dating to Roman era documented by NOAA ROVs.

name: Bowie Seamount
note: Canadian MPA since 2008 — pre-closure trawl scars still visible on sponge reefs centuries old.

name: Davidson Seamount
note: Inside Monterey Bay NMS expansion; bubblegum coral colonies aged to 11,000 years — among Earth's oldest living animals.

name: South Tasman Rise
note: Orange roughy fishery collapsed in <10 years; trawl impact studies show 90% reduction in coral biomass on fished peaks.

name: Lord Howe Rise (Gascoyne)
region: SW Pacific, between Australia and NZ
note: Solitaire and Gascoyne Seamount cluster; New Zealand and Australian deepwater fleets target alfonsino and orange roughy.

name: Hatton Bank
note: Lophelia reefs documented since 1869; UK and Spanish trawlers reduced reef cover by ~70% before 2009 EU partial closure.

name: Suiko Seamount
note: Russian and Japanese fleets historically targeted pelagic armorhead — stock collapsed in 1970s; coral recovery negligible.

name: Sala y Gómez Ridge
region: SE Pacific, west of Easter Island
note: Within Rapa Nui Rahui MPA (2018); fishing pressure on outer flanks remains a flag-of-convenience concern.

name: Burdwood Bank
note: Argentine MPA Yaganes overlap; Chinese and Spanish jiggers / trawlers fish the shelf-edge for toothfish and squid.
